features.clause_structure: main clause plus two of-phrases
features.voice: third person, subject is the study

units.function: Declare the purpose as a search for patterns and bind that search to the policy act it serves.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybersecurity content.
Do not add a second aim in the same sentence; one clause carries one object.
Do not promise a finding here; the clause names a search, not a result.
reusable_elements: aim clause starts the sentence, no first person
the verb is identify, not build or propose
means phrase sits between purpose and object
object is an institution's artefact, not a variable
units.reusable_pattern: This study aims to identify [object: patterns/regularities/drivers] for [means: data-driven X] of [institutional object].
units.rhetorical_move: A single aim clause takes a nominal purpose (identify patterns), qualifies it with a means phrase (for data-driven development), and ends on the institutional object (national policies) so the reader knows who acts on the result.
units.source_excerpt: This study aims to identify patterns for data-driven development and refinement of national cybersecurity policies.

features.clause_structure: main clause plus participial modifier

units.function: Name the paper's own instrument, give it an acronym, and declare how many parts it has before any part is described.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse KDMF or its three sub-models.
Do not describe any sub-model in the same sentence.
Do not state a part count that the later chapters do not follow.
reusable_elements: Specifically marks a step down in generality
acronym invented by the team, expanded on first use
part count stated before any part
units.reusable_pattern: Specifically, we developed the [ABBR] model, consisting of [N] sub-models, to [purpose].
units.rhetorical_move: An adverbial of specification opens the sentence, the acronym follows the expanded name immediately, and a participial phrase fixes the part count so later chapters can be indexed against it.
units.source_excerpt: Specifically, we developed the KDMF model, consisting of three sub-models, to achieve this goal.

features.clause_structure: fronted purpose clause plus main clause
features.quantitative_role: names count of indices through the list length

units.function: Convert a task into an indicator list, with every index named in full and abbreviated in place.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybercrime index set.
Do not justify the indicators here; the sentence reports a choice, not a reason.
Do not exceed four named indices in one sentence.
reusable_elements: purpose clause before the main clause
no justification of the choice in this sentence
units.reusable_pattern: To [task verb] the [object], we selected indicators like [Index A (ABBR)], [Index B (ABBR)], and [Index C].
units.rhetorical_move: A purpose clause fronted by To names the task, the main clause reports the selection, and the list carries full names with bracketed acronyms so the abstract can use the acronyms later.
units.source_excerpt: To analyze the global distribution of cybercrime, we selected indicators like the National Cyber Security Index (NCSI), Cybersecurity Exposure Index (CEI), Legal Measures Index, and Cybercrime Reporting Rate.

features.clause_structure: fronted prepositional phrase plus that-clause

units.function: Report a cluster finding as a comparison between a named high group and its unnamed opposite, with the method fused into the finding sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the Purple Cluster or the cybercrime outcome.
Do not report a number in the same sentence; the number belongs to the results chapter.
Do not name the low group here; it arrives in the next sentence as a contrast.
reusable_elements: cluster is named by colour, not by number
high group carries the positive outcome
no effect size in the sentence
units.reusable_pattern: Through [method 1] and [method 2], we found that [group A] with [attribute], such as those in the [named] Cluster, are better at [outcome].
units.rhetorical_move: A Through phrase names the two methods before the verb, so the result arrives already attributed to its procedure; the comparison is carried by such as those in the Purple Cluster rather than by a separate clause.
units.source_excerpt: Through descriptive analysis and K-means clustering, we found that countries with high NCSI scores and strong legal measures, such as those in the Purple Cluster, are better at preventing and prosecuting cybercrimes.

features.clause_structure: purpose clause plus coordinated object

units.function: Pair two methods in one sentence and assign each a different job, so the reader does not read them as alternatives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse LDA or DID.
Do not explain either method here.
Do not present the pair as a comparison; they are assigned different jobs.
reusable_elements: no statement of which method answers which sub-question
units.reusable_pattern: To assess the [property] of [object], we employed [Method A] and the [Method B] model.
units.rhetorical_move: The purpose clause states the question, and the main clause coordinates two methods whose names are long enough to require acronyms; the coordination itself signals that one classifies and the other tests.
units.source_excerpt: To assess the effectiveness of national cybersecurity policies, we employed Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and the Difference-in-Differences (DID) model.

features.clause_structure: prepositional opener plus copular clause

units.function: Turn the previous finding into a two-valued landscape by naming the opposite group and giving it a risk label.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the Yellow Cluster or the high-risk label.
Do not restate the numbers behind the score.
Do not add a second finding; this sentence only reclassifies the opposite group.
reusable_elements: In contrast opens the sentence and carries the whole comparison
attribute restated as low, not as a number
predicate is a category, not a measurement
units.reusable_pattern: In contrast, [units] in the [named] Cluster with [low attribute] are [risk category].
units.rhetorical_move: A sentence-initial contrast marker stands in for a full comparison; the group is identified by colour and by its low scores, and the predicate replaces an outcome with a threat category.
units.source_excerpt: In contrast, countries in the Yellow Cluster with low scores are high-risk targets.

features.clause_structure: purpose clause plus coordinated methods

units.function: Introduce the third research thread as a correlation question and name both the measure and its check.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse MIC or factor analysis.
Do not report a coefficient value here.
Do not claim causation; the verb is identify the correlation.
reusable_elements: To clause parallel to the earlier method sentences
coefficient named in full then abbreviated
auxiliary method coordinated after the coefficient
units.reusable_pattern: To identify the correlation between [factor class] and [outcome], we used the [Coefficient] method and [auxiliary method].
units.rhetorical_move: A second To clause runs parallel to the earlier method sentences, so the abstract's three questions share one syntax; the main clause names the coefficient and then an auxiliary method, which signals that the coefficient is not trusted alone.
units.source_excerpt: To identify the correlation between demographic factors and cybercrime distribution, we used the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) method and factor analysis.

features.clause_structure: reporting clause plus that-clause

units.function: Open the background with a projected aggregate loss, attributed to reports, so the problem arrives with a price.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the $10.5 trillion figure or the 2025 horizon.
Do not present a projection as a measurement.
Do not stack two intensifiers; one staggering is the whole effect.
reusable_elements: projection verb expected, with a year
units.reusable_pattern: Reports show that the annual global cost of [harm] is expected to reach a staggering $[amount] by [year][n].
units.rhetorical_move: An evidential opener (Reports show) carries a projected figure with a horizon and a citation; the intensifier staggering sits inside the number phrase, where it colours the figure rather than the sentence.
units.source_excerpt: Reports show that the annual global cost of cybercrime is expected to reach a staggering $10.5 trillion by 2025[1].

features.clause_structure: subject plus appositive plus participial phrase
features.quantitative_role: scale word instead of a number
features.tense: past in the example, present in the claim

units.function: Make the aggregate figure concrete with one recent named case whose loss is left vague but large.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cryptocurrency exchange attacks.
Do not give an exact loss for the example; the aggregate figure already carries precision.
Do not introduce a second example in the same sentence.
reusable_elements: cases followed by like, not such as
loss given as a scale word, not a figure
main verb demonstrate with an adverb of clarity
units.reusable_pattern: High-profile cases, like the [year] [incident] causing [scale] losses, clearly demonstrate the [severity] impact.
units.rhetorical_move: An appositive after cases carries the example, a participial phrase states its loss in hundreds of millions rather than an exact figure, and the main verb demonstrative claims the moral of the case.
units.source_excerpt: High-profile cases, like the 2024 cyber-attacks on cryptocurrency exchanges causing hundreds of millions of dollars in losses, clearly demonstrate the severe financial impact.

features.clause_structure: reporting clause plus participial tail
features.quantitative_role: floor rate for an unreported population
features.tense: past in the study, present in the effect

units.function: Argue that the visible problem is smaller than the real one by citing a non-reporting rate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the 60 percent figure.
Do not name a country for the study; the vagueness is what makes it usable.
Do not convert the rate into a count of incidents.
reusable_elements: A study found, not we found
rate is a floor, over not exactly
population is bounded by size or sector
units.reusable_pattern: A study found that over [rate] of [population] in [scope] didn't report [event], hiding the true scale of [threat].
units.rhetorical_move: A study found introduces borrowed evidence; the percentage is attached to a bounded population and a region left deliberately unspecified; the participial tail names what the silence hides.
units.source_excerpt: A study found that over 60% of small-and medium-sized enterprises in a certain region didn't report security breaches, hiding the true scale of cyber threats.

features.clause_structure: three coordinated gerund subjects plus modal predicate

units.function: Convert the three research threads into a single purpose by stacking them as gerunds under one modal claim.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybercrime, policy, demographic triad.
Do not add a fourth gerund; the sentence is built for three.
Do not claim that guidance has been delivered; the modal keeps it prospective.
reusable_elements: each gerund takes a different object class
predicate is modal and evaluative, not factual
no method named in the sentence
units.reusable_pattern: [Gerund 1] the patterns of [X], [gerund 2] the efficacy of [Y], and [gerund 3] the correlations with [Z] can offer invaluable guidance.
units.rhetorical_move: Three gerund phrases, each with its own object, are coordinated before a single predicate; the predicate offers guidance rather than results, which lets the sentence cover all three threads without ranking them.
units.source_excerpt: Comprehending the patterns of cybercrime distribution, evaluating the efficacy of existing policies, and discerning the correlations with national demographics can offer invaluable guidance.

features.clause_structure: verb plus object

units.function: Number the sponsor's tasks in the sponsor's own order, one imperative per bullet, before any method is chosen.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybercrime task wording.
Do not merge two tasks into one bullet.
Do not add commentary to the bullet; expansion belongs to the next paragraph.
reusable_elements: arrow glyph instead of a numeral bullet
units.reusable_pattern: ➢ Task [N]: [Imperative verb] the [deliverable].
units.rhetorical_move: An arrow glyph marks the bullet, the task number is fixed, and the imperative verb opens with no subject; the object of the imperative is the deliverable, not the technique.
units.source_excerpt: ➢ Task 1: Analyze the global distribution of cybercrime.

features.clause_structure: prepositional opener plus copular clause

units.function: Close the background by turning the accumulated alarm into a statement about what policy work is owed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse national cybersecurity policies.
Do not name a specific country or agency in this sentence.
Do not add a third action; the pair is what makes it a genre, not a list.
reusable_elements: predicate is a fixed evaluative phrase
units.reusable_pattern: Against this backdrop, the [action 1] and [action 2] of [object] grounded in [evidence type] are of paramount importance.
units.rhetorical_move: A fixed pivot phrase absorbs the preceding paragraphs, then a nominalised subject (development and refinement) is graded by paramount importance, so the sentence recommends a genre of action without naming an actor.
units.source_excerpt: Against this backdrop, the development and refinement of national cybersecurity policies grounded in data-driven insights are of paramount importance.

features.clause_structure: fronted task phrase plus coordinated verbs and purpose infinitive

units.function: Map each sponsor task onto the method that answers it, one sentence per task, in the sponsor's order.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the K-Means or clustering methods.
Do not skip a task; the paragraph is a map and a gap breaks it.
Do not evaluate the method here.
reusable_elements: For Task N opens the sentence and repeats for each task
actions in the order they were done
method named once inside the list
units.reusable_pattern: For Task [N], we [action 1], [action 2], and used [method] to [purpose].
units.rhetorical_move: A fronted For Task N phrase keys the sentence to the bullet it answers; the main clause lists the actions in execution order, and the final infinitival clause states what the actions produce.
units.source_excerpt: For Task 1, we collected cybercrime data, visualized it, and used K-Means clustering to understand global cybercrime distribution.

features.clause_structure: label plus appositive list plus verb phrase

units.function: Open a score band with a glyph label, then prove the band with three named members and their numbers in place.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the NCSI band or the Belgian example.
Do not give more than three examples; the fourth turns a sample into a list.
Do not explain the score here; explanation follows in the next sentence.
reusable_elements: glyph label carries the band name
score in parentheses after each name
verdict adjective closes without a number
units.reusable_pattern: ➢ [High/Low]-Scoring Countries: Nations such as [Country A (score)], [Country B (score)], and [Country C (score)] exhibit [verdict].
units.rhetorical_move: A bold glyph label names the band, Nations such as fronts the examples, and each country carries its score in parentheses so the reader can see the spread without a table.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 7 of 33 ➢ High-Scoring Countries: Nations such as Belgium (94.81), Lithuania (93.51), and Germany (90.91) exhibit excellent preparedness.

features.clause_structure: appositive list

units.function: Attach the score to the name in parentheses so a ranked list can be read as prose.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the country names or scores.
Do not mix one and two decimal places in the same list.
Do not add a rank number; order already implies it.
reusable_elements: no rank numbers in front of the names
units.reusable_pattern: [Name] ([score to two decimals]), [Name] ([score]), and [Name] ([score])
units.rhetorical_move: The name precedes the number, the number sits in parentheses with two decimals, and the list is closed by and rather than a comma, which signals the end of the band.
units.source_excerpt: Belgium (94.81), Lithuania (93.51), and Germany (90.91)

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus coordinated noun phrases

units.function: Explain a score by listing the institutional capacities it implies, in ascending order of specificity.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybersecurity capacity list.
Do not quantify any capacity here.
Do not claim causation between capacity and score.
reusable_elements: Their points back to the previous sentence's countries
three to four capacities, none quantified
last item is the operational one
units.reusable_pattern: Their high [index] scores reflect [capacity 1], [capacity 2], continuous investment in [domain], and [capacity 3].
units.rhetorical_move: A possessive subject points back to the named countries, reflect makes the score a symptom rather than a measure, and the list runs from strategy to investment to response so the reader infers capability from rank.
units.source_excerpt: Their high NCSI scores reflect comprehensive cybersecurity strategies, well-established policies, continuous investment in cybersecurity infrastructure, and robust incident response mechanisms.

features.clause_structure: given-clause plus main clause plus restating sentence

units.function: Reverse a risk index in public, showing the formula and then restating what the new direction means.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the CEI transformation.
Do not omit the second sentence; a formula alone leaves direction ambiguous.
Do not describe the index as better or worse after reversal.
reusable_elements: second sentence restates the direction in words
no justification of why the reversal is needed
units.reusable_pattern: Given that the original [index] ranges from [a] to [b], with [direction], we transformed the data by calculating [formula]. This new calculation results in a modified [index] where [new direction].
units.rhetorical_move: Given that cites the original range, the transformation is written as a formula the reader can check, and a second sentence states the new meaning so the direction is never ambiguous.
units.source_excerpt: Given that the original CEI ranges from 0 to 1, with higher scores indicating higher exposure to cybercrime, we transformed the data by calculating (1 − 𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑔𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝐶𝐸𝐼 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒) × 100.

features.clause_structure: appositive list

units.function: Report a rate too small to write in decimals by switching to scientific notation and letting the parenthesis carry it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the US or UK figures.
Do not convert to percentages; the notation is the point.
Do not compare two rates of different orders without saying so.
reusable_elements: no verb, the list hangs on the preceding metric sentence
rates not rounded to a common power
units.reusable_pattern: [Country A] ([rate]e-[n]) and [Country B] ([rate]e-[n])
units.rhetorical_move: Country names are coordinated and each carries a rate in scientific notation, so the comparison is made on magnitude rather than on digits; no verb is needed because the list follows a stated metric.
units.source_excerpt: ➢ High Reporting Rates: The United States (2.24e-05) and the United Kingdom (8.88e-06) exhibit relatively high reporting rates, reflecting efficient reporting systems, high public awareness, and trust in authorities.

features.clause_structure: participial phrase

units.function: Attribute a high rate to institutional trust rather than to more crime, which prevents a misreading.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the reporting-system explanation.
Do not turn the participle into a because-clause; the weaker link is deliberate.
Do not add a fourth cause.
reusable_elements: three causes of the same kind
the last cause is the social one
units.reusable_pattern: reflecting [system capacity], [public awareness], and trust in [institution]
units.rhetorical_move: A participial clause opens with reflecting so the cause is attached to the rate without a new subject; three causes are listed, all institutional, and none is measured.
units.source_excerpt: ➢ High Reporting Rates: The United States (2.24e-05) and the United Kingdom (8.88e-06) exhibit relatively high reporting rates, reflecting efficient reporting systems, high public awareness, and trust in authorities.

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus two objects plus result clause

units.function: Report the chosen cluster count as a trade-off outcome rather than as a preference.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the three-cluster result.
Do not claim the choice is correct, only that it was made on two criteria.
Do not omit the second criterion.
reusable_elements: so it was chosen records the consequence
units.reusable_pattern: K = [n] balanced [criterion A] and [criterion B] better, so it was chosen as optimal.
units.rhetorical_move: The equation form K = 3 stands as the subject, the verb balanced takes two criteria as objects, and the closing so it was chosen marks the choice as a consequence instead of a decision.
units.source_excerpt: Although K = 2 had the highest score for cohesion and separation, overall, K = 3 balanced inertia reduction and high Silhouette Score better, so it was chosen as optimal.

features.clause_structure: concessive clause plus main clause

units.function: Admit that a simpler model scored better and defend the more complex choice on a second criterion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the two-versus-three cluster case.
Do not hide the concession; it is what makes the choice credible.
Do not claim the simpler model was wrong.
reusable_elements: the chosen value repeats the criterion that won
units.reusable_pattern: Although K = [m] had the highest [metric A], overall, K = [n] balanced [metric A] and [metric B].
units.rhetorical_move: An Although clause concedes the metric the reader would have picked, the main clause reasserts the chosen value with overall, and balanced carries the argument that two criteria beat one.
units.source_excerpt: Although K = 2 had the highest score for cohesion and separation, overall, K = 3 balanced inertia reduction and high Silhouette Score better, so it was chosen as optimal.

features.clause_structure: label plus reduced clause

units.function: Name a preparation step and its purpose as a labelled bullet, so the method list reads as a checklist.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the standardisation label.
Do not expand the bullet into a paragraph; the list loses its function.
Do not claim the step improved the result.
reusable_elements: label then colon, never a full sentence
purpose stated as comparability, not as a benefit
units.reusable_pattern: [Step label]: [Past participle] [property] across different [dimension] and [dimension].
units.rhetorical_move: The step name precedes a colon, the verb is elided to a past participle, and the purpose is compressed into a noun phrase with no actor.
units.source_excerpt: Data Standardization: Ensured comparability across different scales and units.

features.clause_structure: nominal heading

units.function: Number the findings so a reader can count them, and title each with a noun pair rather than a claim.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybercrime distribution heading.
Do not put a number in the heading.
Do not write the heading as a sentence; it labels the paragraph.
reusable_elements: heading names a topic, not a result
units.reusable_pattern: [n]. [Noun phrase 1] and [Noun phrase 2]
units.rhetorical_move: A numeral and a period open the line, the title coordinates two nouns with and, and no verb appears, which keeps the finding uncommitted until the paragraph that follows.
units.source_excerpt: 1. Cybercrime Distribution and Targeting

features.clause_structure: locative opener plus coordinated subject plus verb

units.function: Use the cluster as a grammatical subject so a descriptive class performs an explanatory role.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the Purple Cluster.
Do not claim the cluster causes the outcome; enable is weaker than cause.
Do not add a third asset.
reusable_elements: cluster named by colour inside a locative phrase
enable as the verb of capability
units.reusable_pattern: In the [colour] Cluster, [asset 1] and [asset 2] enable [outcome].
units.rhetorical_move: A locative phrase opens with In the X Cluster, two institutional assets are coordinated as the subject, and the verb enable converts the description into a capability claim.
units.source_excerpt: ➢ Successful and Thwarted Cybercrimes: In the Purple Cluster, robust cybersecurity infrastructures and stringent legal frameworks enable effective prevention and mitigation of cybercrimes.

features.clause_structure: purpose clause plus main clause plus appositive

units.function: Introduce a borrowed technique by naming the insight problem first and the method second.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse LDA or the topic-modelling description.
Do not evaluate the method in this sentence.
Do not name a second method here.
reusable_elements: to-infinitive names the insight, not the task
no justification of why other methods failed
units.reusable_pattern: To distill [insight type] from these [artefacts], we turned to [Method], a powerful [category] technique in [field].
units.rhetorical_move: An infinitive of purpose states what could not be obtained from the raw text, turned to marks a change of instrument, and an appositive after the method name grades it as powerful so the choice needs no defence.
units.source_excerpt: To distill meaningful insights from these policies, we turned to Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), a powerful topic-modeling technique in natural language processing.

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus quoted list, then separate sentence

units.function: Report a topic model output as a keyword list plus a one-line interpretation of what the topic is about.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cybercrime keyword set.
Do not interpret the topic before listing its keywords.
Do not report the topic weight here.
reusable_elements: keywords quoted, three to four shown
etc. closes the list to avoid transcribing all
units.reusable_pattern: This topic encompasses keywords like "[k1]", "[k2]", "[k3]", etc. It focuses on [referent].
units.rhetorical_move: The topic is the subject, encompasses takes the keyword list in quotes, and a second sentence states the referent in plain institutional language, so the reader gets both the evidence and the label.
units.source_excerpt: The six topics we identified are as follows: ➢ Cybercrime Criminal Legislation: This topic encompasses keywords like "Cybercrime", "warrant", "Penalty", etc.

features.clause_structure: two sentences, first narrative then participial detail

units.function: Report a text pipeline as a temporal sequence of steps with the reason for each step attached.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the stop-word removal detail.
Do not number the steps; the paragraph is narrative.
Do not claim the pipeline improved the result.
reusable_elements: began with fixes the start of the sequence
units.reusable_pattern: Our approach began with [collecting and pre-processing] [artefacts]. This involved [operation 1], including [detail], and [operation 2].
units.rhetorical_move: Our approach began with starts the sequence, involved introduces the operations, and including attaches the rationale as a participial list, so the paragraph reads as a procedure without numbered steps.
units.source_excerpt: Our approach began with collecting and pre-processing a diverse set of national cybersecurity policies.

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus range plus relative clause
features.tense: past perfect in the relative clause

units.function: Justify a treatment group by scarcity, and let the small size stand as the reason rather than as a weakness.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the one-to-two country range.
Do not describe the control group in the same sentence.
Do not soften the small size with an adverb.
reusable_elements: count given as a range, not a total
had implemented, past perfect, marks prior adoption
no apology for the small group
units.reusable_pattern: the experimental group consisted of [n-m] [units] that had implemented [policy]
units.rhetorical_move: The group is the subject, consisted of reports composition, and the number is given as a range so the reader sees how few units adopted the policy; the clause that follows ties the group to the policy year.
units.source_excerpt: For each policy theme, the experimental group consisted of 1-2 countries that had implemented the relevant policies.

features.clause_structure: given-clause plus main clause plus participle
features.voice: active, first person plural with participial tail

units.function: Normalise control variables and give the reason as a property of the model, not of the data.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse min-max normalisation.
Do not give the formula here.
Do not claim normalisation improved fit.
units.reusable_pattern: Given the varying magnitudes of these [variable class], we normalized them using [method], preventing any single variable from [distortion].
units.rhetorical_move: A Given that clause states the problem of scale, the main clause names the method, and a participial clause states what the step prevents, which converts a routine step into a design decision.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 15 of 33 Given the varying magnitudes of these control variables, we normalized them using the min-max normalization method.

features.clause_structure: copular main clause plus adversative clause

units.function: Report a theme-level estimate together with its significance verdict in one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse 0.151 or the 0.05 level.
Do not separate the value and its significance into two sentences.
Do not interpret a null result as evidence of no effect.
reusable_elements: but closes the door on the number
units.reusable_pattern: The [estimator] effect value was [value], but it was not significant (p > [level]).
units.rhetorical_move: The estimator names itself as the subject, the value follows in the past tense, and a but-clause withholds significance immediately, so the reader cannot quote the number without its status.
units.source_excerpt: The Diff-in-Diff effect value was 0.151, but it was not significant ( 𝑝 > 0.05 ), suggesting that the policy in this area had s no discernible impact on cybercrime rates.

features.clause_structure: copular clause plus adjectival phrase plus parenthetical

units.function: Report a significant estimate by pairing the coefficient with its level and its exact p-value.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse 0.708 or p = 0.022.
Do not describe the magnitude as large without a scale.
Do not add a causal claim; the sentence reports an estimate.
reusable_elements: present tense, unlike the null result
units.reusable_pattern: The [estimator] value is [value], significant at the [level] level (p = [p]).
units.rhetorical_move: Present tense marks the estimate as the settled result, significant at the 5% level converts the p-value into a decision, and the exact p is supplied in parentheses for a reader who wants to recompute.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 16 of 33 The Diff-in-Diff value is 0.708, significant at the 5% level ( 𝑝 = 0.022 ).

features.clause_structure: concessive phrase plus main clause plus participial tail

units.function: Rescue a significant estimate from a non-significant pair of components by explaining what the combination means.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the data-protection example.
Do not claim the components were irrelevant; the concession must bite.
Do not give the mechanism without likely.
reusable_elements: concession names the components that failed
estimator named as the surviving quantity
units.reusable_pattern: Despite non-significant [period] Diff values, the significant [estimator] value implies that [policy] are effective in [outcome], likely by [mechanism].
units.rhetorical_move: Despite concedes that neither period moved on its own, the main clause points at the difference of differences, and implies plus a mechanism clause supplies the reading the numbers cannot.
units.source_excerpt: Despite non-significant pre and post-experiment Diff values, the significant Diff-in-Diff value implies that Data Protection and Privacy Regulations are effective in curbing cybercrimes, likely by making data-related crimes more difficult.

features.clause_structure: nominal title

units.function: Title a regression table by naming the method and the exact policy it tests, so the table cannot be reused for another theme.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the data-protection policy name.
Do not summarise the result in the title.
Do not omit the policy name; the table would float free of its theme.
reusable_elements: Results of as the fixed opener
units.reusable_pattern: Results of [Estimator] Analysis of [Policy name]
units.rhetorical_move: Results of opens the title, the estimator is named in full, and Of plus the policy name binds the table to one theme; the title contains no country and no coefficient.
units.source_excerpt: Results of OLS Regression Analysis of Data Protection and Privacy Regulations

features.clause_structure: subject plus modal cause clause plus participial extension

units.function: Explain an unexpected sign by describing the difficulty of the underlying task, not by blaming the data.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the critical-infrastructure example.
Do not attribute the result to data quality.
Do not present the explanation as tested.
reusable_elements: unexpected result names the sign problem
the cause is the task, not the sample
units.reusable_pattern: This unexpected result could be because [task] is a complex task, requiring [condition], and the [policy] may [limitation].
units.rhetorical_move: This unexpected result flags the anomaly, could be because keeps the explanation provisional, and the complementary infinitival clause names a difficulty inherent in the policy area.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 17 of 33 unexpected result could be because protecting critical information infrastructure is a complex task that involves multiple stakeholders and technical challenges.

features.clause_structure: participial phrase plus separate modal clause

units.function: Report a null result and immediately give it a design interpretation rather than leaving it empty.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the emergency-response mechanism.
Do not conclude that the policy does not work.
Do not merge the null and the explanation into one sentence.
reusable_elements: indicating attaches the null to the estimate
second sentence, never the same one
the explanation is about design, not about the policy's value
units.reusable_pattern: ..., indicating no significant impact. This may suggest that the current [mechanism] are not well-designed for [condition].
units.rhetorical_move: A participial indicating states the null, a second sentence with may suggest opens an interpretation that points at the mechanism's design, and the hedging keeps the reading inside the data.
units.source_excerpt: Cybersecurity Incident Emergency Response Mechanisms When considering Cybersecurity Incident Emergency Response Mechanisms, the Diff-in-Diff effect value was-0.189, indicating no significant impact.

features.clause_structure: adverb plus passive clause plus participial list

units.function: Open an extension of the model by marking it as a later step and naming the variables it uses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the factor labels.
Do not report the coefficients here.
Do not justify the step; the chronology is the justification.
units.reusable_pattern: Subsequently, step-by-step [method] analysis was conducted using [Factor 1], [Factor 2], and [Y].
units.rhetorical_move: Subsequently places the step in the paper's chronology, the passive was conducted removes the actor, and the list of factors and the dependent variable fixes exactly what enters the regression.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 19 of 33 Subsequently, step-by-step linear regression analysis was conducted using Factor 1, Factor 2, and 𝑌(the Number of Cyber-crime Incidents (NSCI)).

features.clause_structure: nominal list of pairs

units.function: Report a factor's loading as a run of variable-value pairs inside one line, so the pattern of signs is visible before any table is read.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the variable abbreviations or loadings.
Do not reorder the pairs by magnitude; the given order is the output.
Do not add interpretation inside the line.
reusable_elements: order of pairs implies their importance
units.reusable_pattern: [Factor], [VAR1] [loading], [VAR2] [loading], [VAR3] [loading]
units.rhetorical_move: The factor label opens, then each variable is followed by its signed coefficient with no verb and no connector, and the signs alternate in the line itself.

features.clause_structure: by-phrase plus passive main clause

units.function: Show that the final equation comes from the factor model by naming the substitution that produced it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse Factor Score 1 or the NSCI equation.
Do not present the algebra here.
Do not imply that the derivation was validated by this sentence.
reusable_elements: by plus gerund names the operation
the substituted quantity is named, not written
units.reusable_pattern: By substituting the expression of [factor score] into the [outcome] equation, the final relationship was derived.
units.rhetorical_move: A By plus gerund opens with the operation rather than the result, into names the receiving equation, and the passive derived marks the endpoint, so the derivation is auditable without an appendix.
units.source_excerpt: By substituting the expression of Factor Score 1 into the NSCI equation, the final relationship was derived

features.clause_structure: possessive subject plus verb plus participial cause

units.function: Read one country's coefficient as a country-level story without leaving the sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse Russia's coefficient or its explanation.
Do not state the cause without perhaps.
Do not generalise from one country to the sample.
reusable_elements: country as possessor of the value
shows a strong link, not proves
perhaps due to keeps the cause speculative
units.reusable_pattern: [Country]'s [value] shows a strong link, perhaps due to [cause].
units.rhetorical_move: A possessive country name carries the coefficient, shows a strong link grades it, and perhaps due to introduces a speculative cause that is never tested, which keeps the reading provisional.
units.source_excerpt: For example, Russia' 0.71 shows a strong link, perhaps due to its economic scale and structure.

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus noun phrase plus participial tail

units.function: Flag the single largest association in the table and attribute it to an interpretation in the same sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse Turkey or 0.96.
Do not use strikingly more than once in a section.
Do not convert the association into a causal claim.
reusable_elements: strikingly before the adjective, not before the value
no comparison country in the sentence
units.reusable_pattern: [Country] exhibited a strikingly high [statistic] value of [value], highlighting [interpretation].
units.rhetorical_move: The country is the subject, exhibited is a reporting verb that implies no causation, the adverb strikingly grades the value before it appears, and highlighting attaches the reading.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 20 of 33 ➢ GDP per capita growth: Turkey exhibited a strikingly high MIC value of 0.96, highlighting a close connection between GDP per capita growth and cybercrime, possibly driven by the rapid evolution of network-based economic activities during its growth phase.

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus graded noun phrase

units.function: Rank a variable by its average association and hedge the rank with relatively.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the internet penetration variable.
Do not drop relatively; the variable is not the highest.
Do not compare with a named variable in the same sentence.
units.reusable_pattern: [Variable] demonstrated a relatively high average [statistic] value of [value].
units.rhetorical_move: The variable is the subject, demonstrated a relatively high average value places the statistic between the extreme and the middle, and the comparative is softened so the ranking stays descriptive.
units.source_excerpt: In Russia, the MIC value of 0.65 was relatively lower, implying that GDP per capita growth has a less significant impact on cybercrime, possibly due to its well-established economic and cyber-regulatory frameworks. 6.3.2 Inter-variable Comparative Analysis From the average MIC values, the Internet Penetration Rate demonstrated a relatively high average MIC value of 0.849 with the Number of Cybercrime Cases, underscoring its strong overall association.

features.clause_structure: subject plus verb plus superlative phrase plus participial tail

units.function: Report the weakest variable and immediately limit what its weakness means.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse GDP or 0.3215.
Do not conclude that the variable is irrelevant.
Do not recommend dropping the variable in this sentence.
reusable_elements: four decimals when the value is small
the clause limits the variable's role, not its importance
units.reusable_pattern: [Variable] had the lowest average [statistic] value of [value], suggesting that [narrowed meaning].
units.rhetorical_move: The variable is the subject, had the lowest average states the rank, and suggesting that plus a clause about magnitude narrows the conclusion so low association is not read as irrelevance.
units.source_excerpt: In contrast, GDP had the lowest average MIC value of 0.3215, suggesting that the mere magnitude of GDP has a limited impact on cybercrime, with network-related and economic structural factors likely playing more complex roles. 0.849 0.735 0.682 0.626 0.478 0.3215 IPR GDG AMBS GNC SETE GDP Figure9 MIC values for each variable In summary, different variables exhibit varying degrees of influence across countries, and their average impact levels also diverge.

features.clause_structure: participial clause with parenthetical range

units.function: Describe a perturbation test by stating the allowance given to the parameter, with the range written out.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse beta or the 5 percent allowance.
Do not justify the width in this clause.
Do not report the outcome here.
reusable_elements: range in parentheses with a plus-minus
units.reusable_pattern: allowing [parameter] to fluctuate by [percent] ([centre] ± [half-width]).
units.rhetorical_move: A participial allowing opens the clause, the parameter is named by its Greek symbol, and the range appears in parentheses so the reader can see both the central value and the width.
units.source_excerpt: We selected the fourth group-Cybersecurity Obligations of Network Operators for analysis, allowing 𝛽 to fluctuate by 5% (0.286±0.0143), and plotted the changes in the p-value (which reflects the effect value of significance), and the Diff-in-Diff effect value (before and after the experiment) with the change in 𝛽, as shown in the figure below.

features.clause_structure: main clause plus non-restrictive relative clause
features.quantitative_role: observed bound against a stated expectation

units.function: Close a sensitivity test with a verdict that is a bound rather than an evaluation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the 5 percent bound.
Do not claim robustness beyond the tested range.
Do not omit the expectation clause; the bound alone is not a verdict.
reusable_elements: negative formulation, not is less than
meets expectations, not validates the model
units.reusable_pattern: the change amplitude does not exceed [percent], which meets our stability expectations.
units.rhetorical_move: The amplitude is the subject, does not exceed states the bound as a negative, and the relative clause meets our stability expectations converts the bound into a passed test without claiming accuracy.
units.source_excerpt: Calculations show that the change amplitude does not exceed 5%, which meets our stability expectations and proves that our data selection is reasonable.

features.clause_structure: coordinated main clauses with a purpose infinitive

units.function: Add a second sensitivity test that simulates an adversarial rather than a statistical disturbance.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the hacker framing.
Do not omit the recomputation; the test is the comparison.
Do not report the result here.
reusable_elements: the threat is named in domain terms
no noise level stated in the sentence
units.reusable_pattern: we added random noise to the data to simulate the potential impact of [threat] and then calculated the [statistic] values
units.rhetorical_move: The main clause reports the injection, to simulate names the threat in the paper's own terms (hackers), and then calculated the MIC values restates the measurement so the test is comparable with the baseline.
units.source_excerpt: Therefore, to M verify the robustness and stability of the MIC model, we added random noise to the data to simulate the potential impact of hackers and then calculated the MIC values for the data that might contain outliers and observed the changes in these values.

features.clause_structure: subject plus copular verdict plus locative phrase

units.function: Report that a robustness test left the ranking unchanged by describing the position of the points relative to a reference line.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the six-indicator example.
Do not describe the line by its value; the reader needs the visual anchor.
Do not claim the ranking flips are impossible.
reusable_elements: all weights the sentence toward a uniform result
the reference is described by appearance, not by value
units.reusable_pattern: the new average [statistic] values of the [n] indicators are all stably distributed near the [reference] line
units.rhetorical_move: The recomputed values are the subject, all stably distributed is the verdict, and near the gray dotted line names the visual reference, so the claim is tied to a figure the reader is looking at.
units.source_excerpt: If the end of the ring exceeds the gray asymptote, the new MIC value is higher than the previous one.As expected, the new average MIC values of the six indicators are all stably distributed near the gray dotted line, indicating that the robustness and stability of the MIC model are quite remarkable.

features.clause_structure: nominal heading

units.function: Open a strength block with a numeral and a hyphenated adjective-noun title that names the virtue.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the data-driven analysis title.
Do not claim a strength that the paragraph does not evidence.
Do not use more than one adjective.
reusable_elements: hyphenated compound as the evaluative load
units.reusable_pattern: [n]. [Compound adjective]-[noun] [Analysis/Design]
units.rhetorical_move: A numeral, a hyphenated compound adjective, and a noun title state the strength in three words, and the paragraph that follows must supply the evidence.
units.source_excerpt: 1. Comprehensive Data-Driven Analysis

features.clause_structure: main clause plus non-restrictive relative clause

units.function: Claim originality by naming the act of invention and then stating what the invention combines.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the KDMF name.
Do not claim novelty for a single sub-model.
Do not leave the integration clause out; it is the evidence for the claim.
reusable_elements: the adverb sits between subject and verb
units.reusable_pattern: We creatively came up with the [ABBR] model, which integrated these [n] sub-models and provided [affordance].
units.rhetorical_move: We creatively frames the model as an act rather than a choice, came up with keeps the register plain, and the relative clause states the integration so the novelty is locatable.
units.source_excerpt: Advanced Analytical Methods ➢ We creatively came up with the KDMF model, which integrated these four sub-models and provided a holistic view of cybercrime.

features.clause_structure: copular verdict plus by-phrase plus modal clause

units.function: Defend the choice of an estimator by naming the inferential problem only it solves.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse DID or the causal-effect claim.
Do not defend a method without naming the comparison it enables.
Do not call a descriptive method indispensable.
reusable_elements: proves indispensable, a verdict not a preference
precisely isolates names the inferential gain
units.reusable_pattern: the [Estimator] model proves indispensable. By comparing [group A] with [group B], it can precisely isolate [quantity].
units.rhetorical_move: The estimator is the subject, proves indispensable is a strong verdict, and the By plus gerund clause states the comparison that produces the causal reading, so the defence is procedural rather than rhetorical.
units.source_excerpt: ➢ When evaluating the impact of national security policies on cybercrime rates, the DID model proves indispensable.

features.clause_structure: by-phrase plus passive modal main clause

units.function: Claim that two methods agree, and treat the agreement itself as the evidence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse MIC and factor analysis.
Do not claim the methods are independent if they share inputs.
Do not report agreement without the cross-check in the same sentence.
reusable_elements: the checking method comes second in the sentence but first in the clause
identified by names the source of the claim
units.reusable_pattern: By using [method B] to cross-check the relationships identified by [method A], the conclusions drawn from both methods can be mutually validated.
units.rhetorical_move: A By plus gerund names the checking method, identified by factor analysis points back to the first result, and the main clause states that the conclusions are cross-validated without reporting a number.
units.source_excerpt: By using MIC to cross-check the relationships identified by factor analysis, we can ensure that all possible relationships, whether simple linear ones or complex non-linear ones, are thoroughly explored.

features.clause_structure: since-clause plus modal main clause

units.function: State a data limitation as a selection rule and derive the direction of the bias from it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse VCDB or the disclosure rule.
Do not state a bias without its direction.
Do not quantify the bias here.
reusable_elements: Since opens with the rule, not with an apology
only includes is the operative restriction
units.reusable_pattern: Since [database] only includes [inclusion rule], it may lead to an [direction] of [quantity].
units.rhetorical_move: Since names the inclusion rule, only includes marks the boundary, and may lead to an under-estimation states the direction of the error rather than merely its existence.
units.source_excerpt: Since VCDB only includes publicly disclosed data breaches, it may lead to an under-estimation of the actual number of cyber threats. 2.

features.clause_structure: subject plus modal verb plus object plus as-clause

units.function: Name a modelling limitation by describing what the method cannot represent, not by saying it is imperfect.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse K-means or the clustering criticism.
Do not criticise the method without naming what it flattens.
Do not propose the fix in the same sentence.
reusable_elements: the object is named as a relationship, not as data
the mechanism is stated after the verdict
units.reusable_pattern: [Method] analysis may oversimplify the complex relationships between [X] and [Y], as it [mechanism].
units.rhetorical_move: The method is the subject, may oversimplify is a modal verdict, and the complex relationships clause states the specific object the method flattens, which makes the criticism technical.
units.source_excerpt: Model-related Constraints ➢ K-clustering analysis may oversimplify the complex relationships between different factors contributing to cybercrime distribution.

features.clause_structure: coordinated noun list plus passive modal predicate

units.function: List unmodelled confounders as a flat noun series and disclaim them in one clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cultural or political confounders.
Do not explain how any confounder would change the result.
Do not list more than four.
reusable_elements: may not be accounted for, passive
units.reusable_pattern: [Confounder 1], [confounder 2], or [confounder 3] ... may not be accounted for in the model.
units.rhetorical_move: Three abstract nouns are coordinated, or opens alternatives within the list, and may not be accounted for in the model closes the sentence with the scope admission in the passive.
units.source_excerpt: Cultural differences, political stability, or law enforcement efficiency, which can influence cybercrime rates, may not be accounted for in the model.

features.clause_structure: nominal heading with colon expansion

units.function: Open a future-work block with a numeral, a gerund heading, and a colon that lists the two operations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the data-quality direction.
Do not promise a result in the heading.
Do not list more than two operations in the heading.
units.reusable_pattern: [n]. [Gerund] [Object]: [Operation 1] and [Operation 2]
units.rhetorical_move: The numeral orders the direction, the gerund nominalises the action so it reads as a programme, and the colon expands it into two coordinated operations.
units.source_excerpt: 1. Augmenting Data Quality: Expansion and Standardization

features.clause_structure: subject plus modal verb plus purpose infinitive

units.function: Recommend a direction with a modal and a metaphor that implies the present sample was narrow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the wider-net image.
Do not address the recommendation to the team.
Do not promise that the extension would change the result.
reusable_elements: one metaphor, then a literal purpose
units.reusable_pattern: Future studies should [verb metaphor] to [purpose] from [source class].
units.rhetorical_move: Future studies is the agent, should carries the recommendation, and cast a wider net supplies the image, which is then cashed out by an infinitive naming the source diversity wanted.
units.source_excerpt: Augmenting Data Quality: Expansion and Standardization Future studies should cast a wider net to gather data from diverse sources.

features.clause_structure: passive modal clause

units.function: Turn the paper's heterogeneity finding into a design principle for the reader.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the national-context wording verbatim.
Do not name a country in this sentence.
Do not turn the principle into a specific recommendation.
units.reusable_pattern: [policies] must be tailored to specific [context] contexts.
units.rhetorical_move: The object is the subject, must carries obligation rather than possibility, and tailored to specific contexts names the reason in the same breath as the rule.
units.source_excerpt: In addition, given the disparities in cybercrime distribution and policy effectiveness among countries, policies must be tailored to specific national contexts.

features.clause_structure: field label plus nominal phrase

units.function: Address the memo to a named audience at a named event, so the reader knows the register before the first sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the ITU summit.
Do not address individuals by name.
Do not add a salutation line; the field label is the salutation.
reusable_elements: audience named by role, not by name
units.reusable_pattern: To: [audience role] attending the upcoming [event]
units.rhetorical_move: To plus colon names the readers by role and by occasion, and the event supplies the deadline, which justifies the memo's brevity.
units.source_excerpt: To: Country leaders attending the upcoming ITU Summit on Cybersecurity

features.clause_structure: main clause plus with-phrase

units.function: Re-announce the problem in the memo with the same aggregate figure, compressed and stripped of citation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the $10.5 trillion figure in the memo.
Do not repeat the incident example.
Do not add a second statistic to the same sentence.
reusable_elements: citation dropped because the memo is short
units.reusable_pattern: In the [period], [topic] has emerged as a significant threat, with an expected annual [cost] of $[amount] by [year].
units.rhetorical_move: The topic is the subject, has emerged marks arrival rather than existence, and with plus a nominal phrase carries the cost figure and its horizon without a reference.
units.source_excerpt: Team # 2513705 Page 25 of 33 Memorandum To: Country leaders attending the upcoming ITU Summit on Cybersecurity From: Team 2513705 Date: January 27, 2025 Subject: Insights on National Cybersecurity Policies for ITU Summit In the digital age, cybercrime has emerged as a significant threat, with an expected annual global cost of $10.5 trillion by 2025.

features.clause_structure: labelled fields

units.function: Summarise one research area as an area label followed by an approach label, so the memo can be skimmed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the distribution or clustering labels.
Do not explain the method in the memo.
Do not put two methods under one Approach label.
reusable_elements: method named in three words or fewer
units.reusable_pattern: [Area]: ➢ Approach: [Method]
units.rhetorical_move: The area name heads the line with a colon, a glyph marks the sub-field, and Approach names the method in three words or fewer; the finding follows in a separate clause.
units.source_excerpt: Cybercrime Distribution ➢ Approach: K-Means

features.clause_structure: fronted authorising phrase plus main clause with infinitive

units.function: Convert the findings into an instruction with a single transition phrase and a ranked first action.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the data-protection recommendation.
Do not recommend more than two actions in one sentence.
Do not qualify the recommendation with if budget allows.
units.reusable_pattern: Based on our findings, we recommend to prioritize [action 1] and [action 2].
units.rhetorical_move: Based on our findings authorises the move, we recommend takes an infinitive, and prioritize ranks the actions so the memo ends with an order rather than a summary.
units.source_excerpt: Based on our findings, we recommend to prioritize strengthening data protection and privacy regulations, enhancing network operator security obligations, and clarifying cross-border data flow rules.

features.clause_structure: adverb plus thanks clause, then main clause with that-clause

units.function: Close the memo by acknowledging the reader's time and leaving one forward-looking claim.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the memo wording verbatim.
Do not add a request in the closing.
Do not claim that the findings are final.
reusable_elements: the claim is about the project, not the paper
no new evidence in the closing
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, thank you for reading our [document] in your busy schedule. We believe that this project will have a [effect].
units.rhetorical_move: Finally marks the last move, the thanks are tied to the reader's constraint (in your busy schedule), and the closing claim about the project's future value gives the memo a horizon.
units.source_excerpt: Finally, thank you for reading our memo in your busy schedule.
